item.title: The Black Crowes’ Chris Robinson Addresses Backlash Over Onstage Comments
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: Welcome to our podcast, where we dive into the latest music news. Today, we're talking about The Black Crowes and the controversy surrounding their recent performance in Tampa.
[Short music transition]
Host: On May 31st, the band was performing at the MidFlorida Credit Union Amphitheatre as part of their Southern Hospitality tour. After playing "Soul Singing," some fans started chanting "U-S-A!" apparently prompted by the band's mascot dressed as Uncle Sam on the screen behind them. Lead singer Chris Robinson responded from the stage, saying "Thanks for the geography lesson. I don’t know what you’re so proud of right now." He also stated, "Some of us have real faith. For those of you f—–g booing us, some of us are not afraid. And we most assuredly are not f—–g ignorant."
[Short music transition]
Host: The exchange led to some crowd members walking out, and the incident has sparked a lot of discussion. Chris Robinson recently spoke to Ultimate Classic Rock to provide some context, saying the whole thing was "blown out of context" to stir up controversy. He also made it clear that he has respect for veterans and those who have made sacrifices, but feels the need to speak his mind and make a connection with people through his music.
[Short music transition]
Host: This incident is particularly notable given the timing, just days after Memorial Day. The Black Crowes have a new album out, "A Pound of Feathers," and are continuing their Southern Hospitality tour with upcoming dates in Augusta and Charlotte.
[Outro music plays]
Host: That's all for today. Thanks for tuning in, and we'll catch you in the next episode.
